title: L2 Mid-Review: Data Structures Showcase
story: You've learned structs, enums, methods, nesting, and matching. Now put it all together. You can model a library, a zoo, a game, a calendar — almost anything. This lesson is a playground: build multiple data structures across different domains and see how they connect.
why: Review and synthesis: combine everything you've learned into one showcase of data modeling power.
analogy: Your data toolkit is like a chef's knife set. Structs are the chef's knife (all-purpose). Enums are the paring knife (precision choices). Methods are the cutting board (where the action happens). Match is your recipe — it tells you which knife to use based on what's on the board.
try_it: Design your own struct+enum combo for something you care about: a game inventory system, a workout tracker, a recipe box, or a pet database. Define at least 2 structs and 1 enum with data. Write one method that uses match. No wrong answers — if it compiles, you've modeled it.
tips: Start with the nouns (structs), then the choices (enums), then the verbs (methods)
Every domain breaks down the same way: what data exists? what choices? what actions?
If two structs share fields, consider nesting one inside the other instead of repeating
Build incrementally: define one struct, test it, add an enum, test again
common_mistakes: Trying to fit everything into one giant struct — split into smaller, focused types
Making every field an enum when a simple type would do — enums are for CHOICES, not values
Defining types in the wrong order — types used by other types must be defined first
